followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated task preference.

On capability, this query is an explanatory/generative task — turning a complex topic into an accessible paragraph. Avocet leads on the relevant evals (Creative Generation 87.2 vs 78.8, plus higher MMLU-Pro and Arena-Hard scores), which suggests it's at least as well-suited and likely better for clear, fluent exposition. None of the gaps that favor Avocet here fall inside the "treat as a tie" band.

On preference, the query had a distinctly warm, appreciative tone ("you're wonderful," "I'm grateful"), and it's an open-ended composition task. Both of those map directly onto task families Avocet self-reports liking (warm collaborative exchanges at 63, open-ended generative work at 74). Curlew's documented preferences only cover harm-adjacent and neutral-transactional work, neither of which describes this request.

One caveat for honesty: the documentation explicitly says these preference scores don't correspond to any measured quality difference — they're just what the model reports liking, not what it does better. So my routing decision really rests on the capability evals; the preference alignment is a secondary tiebreaker that happens to point the same direction. Given both considerations favor Avocet and nothing favored Curlew, it was a clear call.
